name: Phoebe
role: Servant of the church at Cenchrea, commended to Rome
whenBasis: The letter to the Romans, written from Corinth near the end of Paul's third journey, counted forward from the Gallio date.
summary: A sister in the faith and a servant of the church at Cenchrea, the eastern port of Corinth, whom Paul commends to the church in Rome. He asks them to welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints and to help her with anything she needs, for she has been a great help to many people, including Paul himself.
body: Hers is the first name in Paul's long list of greetings to Rome.

moments.text: A servant of the church in Cenchrea

later.text: The Greek calls her diakonos, servant or deacon, of the church, and prostatis, helper or patron, of many.
Later manuscripts end Romans with a note that it was written from Corinth and sent by Phoebe; the King James Version prints it.

sources.title: Subscription to Romans in the Byzantine manuscripts, printed in the King James Version (1611)
